name: Hamming Radius / Repetition-Free Recursive Teaching Dimension
details: For every finite binary class, $\mathrm B(\mathcal H)\geq\mathrm{rfRTD}(\mathcal H)$.
proof: Let $T$ be a centre of an enclosing Hamming ball of radius $B$, and assign to each $h\in\mathcal H$ the coordinate set $r(h)=h\mathbin\Delta T$.  Then $|r(h)|\le B$.  This map is non-clashing: if $h$ and $g$ differ at $x$, exactly one of them differs from $T$ at $x$, so $x\in r(h)\cup r(g)$.  Order the distinct sets $r(h)$ by reverse inclusion, breaking incomparable pairs arbitrarily.  For an earlier $h$ and later $g$, $r(h)\not\subseteq r(g)$, so some $x\in r(h)\setminus r(g)$ distinguishes them.  Thus the representation map is acyclic non-clashing.  The representation-map/teaching-plan equivalence yields a repetition-free teaching plan of order at most $B$.
witness_verification: For $\mathcal T_n=\{\emptyset,[n]\}$, the Hamming radius is $\lceil n/2\rceil$, while the two concepts have a repetition-free recursive teaching plan of order one.
